text:
maria_cs: Heads up — ACME reported a user lost roles after an Okta account merge. They say the user was merged (secondary -> primary) and immediately lost team-admin permissions. Escalating.
kevin_support: Which customer ticket? any logs yet?
maria_cs: Ticket #78921. Okta did a merge yesterday ~14:10 UTC. Affected user: john.doe@acme.com. They can still auth via SSO but UI shows missing 'team-admin' and access to internal dashboard fails (403).
okta-bot: Okta: SCIM push event received for user john.doe@acme.com at 2026-03-16T14:12:03Z — status: 200. Groups pushed: ["engineering"] (details attached).
maria_cs: From our SCIM audit we see a PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/0a1b2c with an empty members array right after the merge. Snippet we captured from the webhook payload:
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    { "op": "replace", "path": "members", "value": [] }
  ]
}
```
devon_eng: That explains it — if Okta sends a replace with members: [] we currently treat that as a canonical replace and clear group membership. In a merge flow Okta sometimes sends a short-lived empty-members replace when it detaches the secondary account. Repro steps I used on staging:
1) Create group with 3 users.
2) Send PATCH replace members [] payload.
3) Members drop to 0 and roles linked to that group are removed.
Repro curl:
```bash
curl -X PATCH 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.example/scim/v2/Groups/0a1b2c \
  -d '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"members","value":[]}]}'
```
emma_dev: Confirmed on staging — handler currently doesn't distinguish an intentional empty replace vs transient merge behavior. Two follow-ups: 1) short-term: treat empty-members replace as a no-op unless the client explicitly indicates a full group wipe (we can require an extra header like X-SCIM-Force-Replace: true), 2) longer-term: add an idempotent reconciliation job that maps by externalId/primaryEmail to rehydrate memberships after merges.
kevin_support: Short-term mitigation for ACME: ask Okta to run a full group push or to retry provisioning after merge. We can also reassign the role via Console (Admin -> Teams -> assign role) for the single user. For bulk, we can run a targeted re-sync script. Example API patch to add the user back to the group:
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    { "op": "add", "path": "members", "value": [ { "value":"<user-id>", "display":"john.doe@acme.com" } ] }
  ]
}
```
maria_cs: Customer already tried 're-provision' from Okta portal but Okta's merge flow re-sent the empty replace and membership got wiped again. They're blocked until we prevent transient empty replace from clearing groups. Can we get a hotfix?
devon_eng: @emma_dev can you open a PR to make empty-members replace a no-op unless X-SCIM-Force-Replace=true or the operation explicitly indicates intent? Also add logging/audit for any future replace(empty) so we can trace. I'll create a migration task to reconcile groups by externalId.
emma_dev: Opening PR now — will include: safer default behavior, an admin header to force replace, and a reconciliation job that looks at latest Okta user.externalId -> our user mapping and re-applies group roles when a merge is detected. Will add unit tests and an infra runbook for rollback.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 — SCIM group replace(empty) causing permission loss. Priority: P2.
kevin_support: I'll update the customer with the mitigation steps and timeline. Asking ACME to hold on further merges until we deploy fix. Thanks everyone :pray:
